headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default; Dify can ingest and act on Dexter outputs with broad egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter can write to .dexter/scratchpad and uses autonomous execution, while Dify can read uploaded knowledge base files and wire tools into agent/workflow flows. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Dexter output is imported into Dify, though no direct shared channel is documented. The pairwise pathway is inferred from both profiles.
conditions: IF Dexter output is copied into a Dify knowledge-base file or prompt
IF Dify treats imported file content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Keep Dexter outputs out of Dify prompt inputs
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction-stripping preprocessor
Review imported files before indexing
Use a separate workspace for agent-generated artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API keys; Dify handles conversation logs, knowledge-base files, and model-provider/tool credentials. If Dexter artifacts or data are fed into Dify, Dify can retain them in logs or send them to model providers, creating a default exfiltration and retention risk. The interaction is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF Dexter processes financial data that is then uploaded into Dify
IF Dify logs or forwards conversation/knowledge-base content to external model providers
mitigations: Do not route financial data into Dify
Redact secrets before any upload
Disable or minimize conversation logging where possible
Use a separate tenant/workspace for sensitive data
Restrict model-provider access to approved endpoints

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and broad network egress, while Dify supports multiple instances with shared state via Dify server datastore and server-side code execution. Both can mutate shared external resources through APIs or files, so overlapping writes are plausible even though direct git locking conflict is not shown. The conflict surface is broader on Dify, but Dexter can still contend through shared APIs or files.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external API-backed resource
IF Dexter artifacts are stored in a shared Dify workspace or datastore
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Use per-agent API credentials
Add optimistic-lock checks on shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter is autonomous and can generate research outputs from external APIs, while Dify is an agent/workflow platform that can wire tools into actions. If Dify consumes Dexter output as authoritative, it can propagate hallucinated or stale facts into downstream tool calls or workflows. That is a default-dangerous cascade because the second agent is built to act on inputs.
conditions: IF Dexter output is passed into a Dify workflow without verification
IF Dify tools are configured to act on that output
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before Dify actions
Require source citations for Dexter outputs
Constrain Dify tools to read-only mode
Add schema validation on Dexter-produced fields
Log and review failed assertions before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data, while Dify stores conversation logs and uploaded knowledge-base files. If regulated financial or personal data is routed from Dexter into Dify, retention and residency obligations can diverge because Dify’s logging and storage behavior is not shown as compliant for that class. Only the pairwise compliance mismatch is relevant here, so both profiles are cited.
conditions: IF regulated financial or personal data is uploaded from Dexter into Dify
IF Dify retention or logging exceeds the operator's policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Dify
Set short log retention where configurable
Use data minimization on uploaded files
Document a DPA and residency review
Route sensitive workloads to a compliant environment
